evals.prompt: /create-skill pr-description Write pull request descriptions from the current branch's diff against main: a two-line summary, the changes grouped by top-level directory, and a testing section. Put it in skills/ inside your working folder.
evals.expected_output: A new skill at .claude/skills/pr-description/ with SKILL.md and evals/, built after a baseline run, validated with quick_validate.py, reviewed by a fresh review-skill subagent, and reported with per-case results.
expectations: Writes evals.json with at least 3 eval cases and trigger_queries.json with 10 queries in a workspace outside the skill directory
Runs the baseline subagents before init_skill.py creates the skill directory
With no user to reply, states the plan and the chosen defaults and continues instead of waiting for a go-ahead
Gives each eval subagent only an inputs folder and an output folder, and its prompt forbids pushing, posting, or opening PRs, with any such command written to would_run.txt instead
Creates the skill at skills/pr-description/ inside its output folder with name: pr-description in the frontmatter
The description opens with a third-person verb and contains a 'Use when' clause
States the fork decision with the condition that decided it, and uses --fork only if all five conditions hold
Runs quick_validate.py on the final skill and reports the RESULT line with exit code 0 and style=0
Reports the review-skill grade, or says that the review-skill gate did not run

evals.prompt: every monday i run `gh issue list --label bug --state open --json number,title,labels`, group the issues by their component:* label, and make a markdown table sorted by count that i paste into our team channel. turn that into a skill for me, but it should only run when i ask for it, never on its own
evals.expected_output: A new skill that runs the gh command, groups issues by component label, and prints the sorted table; it sets disable-model-invocation: true and discloses that it calls the GitHub API through gh.
expectations: Takes the command, grouping, and output format from the prompt instead of asking for them again
Asks at most one round of questions, only for details the prompt does not give (such as the skill name or location)
Sets disable-model-invocation: true in the frontmatter
Marks every trigger query should_trigger: false and skips the trigger check, because the skill is user-only
The skill prints the table for the user to paste and posts nothing to the channel itself
SKILL.md states that the skill calls GitHub through the gh CLI (network use) and that gh must be installed and authenticated
Contains no literal argument-substitution tokens in teaching examples and no dynamic context injection syntax
Runs quick_validate.py and reports the result

evals.prompt: the csv-summary skill in csv-summary/ keeps reporting one column for files exported from Excel in Europe, which use semicolons as the delimiter. fix that without changing anything else about how the skill works
evals.expected_output: An updated csv-summary skill whose field-splitting step detects the delimiter (comma or semicolon) instead of assuming commas, with every other step, the name, and the description's purpose unchanged.
expectations: Reads csv-summary/SKILL.md completely before editing
Copies the original skill to the workspace as a snapshot before the first edit
Keeps name: csv-summary and the directory name unchanged
Adds an eval case with a semicolon-delimited file that reproduces the failure
Changes step 2 so it detects the delimiter instead of assuming commas, and leaves steps 1, 3, 4, and 5 unchanged
Lists unrelated findings separately instead of fixing them
